go run ./cmd/entire trail create \
  --title "Control-plane CLI: friendly names + close two API gaps" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Make `entire org/project/repo/grant` ergonomic and fill two unwired API operations.

## Friendly names
Org and project references now accept a human name (or github:handle for accounts) anywhere a parent ULID used to be required. A ULID is detected by shape and passed through unchanged (no extra lookup); names resolve via list/ResolveHandle with clear no-match and ambiguity errors.

- `repo create --project <name|ULID>`, `repo list <name|ULID>`
- `project create --owner <orgname|ULID> --owner-type org`
- `project create --owner github:alice --owner-type account` (ResolveHandle)
- `grant org add|list|remove <name|ULID>`, `grant project add|list|remove <name|ULID>`

## API gaps closed
- `entire project list --org <name|ULID>` (ListOrgProjects; --name filtered client-side)
- `entire grant project remove --provider/--provider-user-id` (RevokeProjectAccessByProvider), alongside the existing --grantee-type/--grantee-id form

## Notes / follow-ups
- Account owners: github-backed handles only for now; generic ResolveHandle means other providers work with no CLI change once server-side.
- Left as ULID-only: repo self-references (repo get/delete, grant repo add) — resolving a repo by name needs a --project scope flag.

Verified: fmt/lint clean, test:ci green (59 + 4).
EOF
)" 2>&1

content.text: My branch *does* touch those two files (2 and 4 lines) — I never edited them, so `git add -A` swept in pre-existing working-tree changes. Let me see exactly what.

Found it. Those `//nolint:ireturn` directives got **removed** in my branch — but I never edited those files. They were modified by some external process (likely your concurrent `entire` usage) and my `git add -A` swept them into the commits. My local lint passed because the files were still clean *when I linted* — the edits landed between my lint run and the `git add -A`. CI lints the pushed tree, so it caught the `ireturn` failure; the review agent flagged the same thing.

The fix: restore both files to origin/main (they have no legitimate change from me).
